newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Chinese tin miners diversify as prices ease.
newsitem.headline: Chinese tin miners diversify as prices ease.

text.p: Chinese tin mining companies, prompted by lower prices, are diversifying into zinc, lead, antimony and even chemicals, said Wang Bibo, general manager of Kinmet Non-Ferrous Metals.
"In the next few years there will be almost no single tin producers, even Yunan Tin," Bibo told a conference organised by the International Tin Research Institute.
Bibo said that the tin industry was having to adopt this strategy in the face of over-capacity, shortage of reserves and low demand.
State owned tin companies were experiencing increasing financial difficulties and may have to privatise in the near future, he added.
But the increasingly influential private sector, which accounts for half the tin industry, is fragmented into a large number of small producers.
"We hope they can unite together to achieve something in future," he said.
Earlier, the deputy general manager of Yunnan tin Corp, Xu Qiren, disclosed that China produced 67,659 long tons of tin products and 5.2 million long tons of tin ore in 1995.
Production capacities are 116,600 long tons and 12.35 million long tons respectively, he added.
Yunnan Tin Corp has a tin mining capacity of 4.0 million long tons a year and smelting capacity of 25,000 long tons a year.
It also produces lead, copper, zinc, antimony and other non-ferrous metals.
Xu Qiren forecast Chinese tin consumption growing gradually in line with the Chinese economy to between 28,000 and 30,000 long tons in 2000, from between 22,000 and 23,000 long tons in 1996.
